newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish govt lowers inflation forecast for 96/97.
newsitem.headline: Swedish govt lowers inflation forecast for 96/97.

text.p: The Swedish government, in its 1997 budget, lowered its forecast for the consumer price index in 1996 to 1.0 percent against an April forecast of 1.9 percent.
The government also revised its forecast for 1997 to 2.2 percent from 2.3 percent five months ago.
"Inflation in Sweden has to date this year been considerably lower than what was expected in spring," the Finance Ministry said in a statement.
"The low rate of inflation is explained by, amongst other things, lower import prices, falling interest rates and tax changes."
The ministry said increases in productivity had also been higher than expected.
"The relatively rapid wage ioncreases will probably result in rationalisation initiatives which will hold down prices," it said.

The ministry said the inflation rate as measured by the consumer price index would increase during 1997 because it was anticipated that the crown would not appreciate further, and interest rates will not fall.
"Towards the end of 1997, inflation will be in the vicinity of the two percent inflationary target of the Riksbank (central bank)," the ministry said.
It said underlying inflation, measured by the CPI adjusted for changes in the exchange rate, interest rate and taxes, would be stable in 1996 and 1997 and close to two percent.
"On the other hand it is expected that underlying inflation, measured as wages increases less than the trend for increases in productivity, will decline from 1996 to 1997."
The government forecast the CPI steady at 2.2 percent in 1998, 1999 and 2000.
